Subject: Post-demo: BrightDesk model-fit & fn-call qualification

Hi Sara / Ethan — thanks again for joining the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared context:  

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: extract structured ticket metadata (category, priority, SLA, product area) from free-form support emails and route to internal triage.
- Volume: ~18k tickets/month, median ticket length ~220 tokens, ~8% contain code snippets.
- Key constraint: Customer data must not persist beyond request lifetime in hosted eval; production will be either Dedicated or Private.

Redwood recommendations (high level)
- Pilot models: try a 7B quantized LLM optimized for structured output (recommended: redwood-alpha-7b-q4f) and a higher-capacity 13B variant for edge cases (redwood-beta-13b-q4f).
- Function calling: build a single fn-call schema for ticket fields and a fallback plain-text parser for unknowns.
- Quality/regression guardrails: record a 1k prompt-set baseline and run nightly scorers; alert on >5% drop in exact-match for high-priority fields.

Attachments sent with this thread: brightdesk_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts + expected JSON), benchmark-summary-2028-09.csv (quick perf/latency sketch), brightdesk_fncall_schema_v2.json (proposed callable schema).

Proposed immediate next steps
1) We (Redwood) run a 48-hour sandbox with both model variants on a 1000-example prompt slice (we'll use the attached prompt set).
2) Marissa will run the structured-output + fn-call compliance checks and share a compliance report with schema pass/fail and retry behavior notes.
3) Dylan will prepare an initial latency/cost estimate for Dedicated and Hosted modes.
4) BrightDesk to confirm any restricted data fields and contract timeline.

Can you confirm you’re ok with the sandbox window (start: Tue 2028-09-13) and share any additional do-not-send tokens or IP rules?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jasmine — a few concrete notes from the eval/QA side after reviewing the sample prompt set:  

Model recommendations (detailed)
- redwood-alpha-7b-q4f: strong with short tickets and structured templates; average token latency ~18ms/token on A100; best first pass for cost-sensitive production.
- redwood-beta-13b-q4f: markedly better on code snippets and multi-paragraph context (improves exact-match for 'product_area' by ~7% in our bench). Use as a fallback tier.

JSON schema & retry guidance
- The attached brightdesk_fncall_schema_v2.json has a strict enum for 'category' and an optional free_text for 'notes'. We recommend a two-step retry policy: 
  1) If the fn-call response fails schema validation, automatically re-run with increased temperature 0.2 and expanded context (add the previous assistant output as context).
  2) If second attempt fails, fallback to a regex-based extractor and flag ticket for manual triage.

Benchmarks and pass criteria
- We'll run three passes over the 1k sample: structural compliance (JSON schema pass rate >= 92%), field-level exact match for (category, priority, product_area) >= 88%, latency p95 < 300ms for the 7b model in Hosted.

Data residency & PII note
- For the sandbox we will redact any long snippets that contain full credit-card numbers or SSNs; please note if BrightDesk requires additional PII masking rules.

I'll start the schema compliance harness tomorrow and will share the first compliance table by EOD Wed.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior ML Engineer, Inference QA

Hi Jasmine / Marissa — this all looks good, thanks for the rapid follow-up. A couple clarifications from our side:  

1) Sandbox window: Tue 9/13 works. Please ensure no logs are retained in hosted mode — we need ephemeral handling during the eval.
2) PII rules: redact account numbers and any internal customer IDs (we'll provide a list); free_text notes can remain if redacted.
3) Quality/regression concern: historically we see regressions when the training data includes lots of HTML fragments — will your schema harness detect and flag HTML-induced tokenization failures?

Also: for the fn-call schema, can you include an example of the exact callable payload we should expect (including types/enum values) so our engineers can test integration with our routing microservice?

If you can share a short sample run (20 examples) with both models by EOD Thu, that would help unblock our engineering spike next week.

Thanks,
